static_traits.name: Chen Hao
static_traits.family_status: Mother works as a palm reader in New Orleans
static_traits.social_status: Tense relationships with friends, rarely meeting friends due to spending most time at the casino; although having friends to confide in, not yet disclosing the gambling problem to them due to shame and embarrassment
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; never had similar problems before, never received psychotherapy
static_traits.language_features: Self-deprecation, negative skepticism; can clearly describe problems and consequences, logic basically clear; skeptical about counseling effectiveness but willing to try; expresses shame and a sense of failure

basic_info.main_problem: Feeling like a failure and ashamed because of spending too much at the casino; these problems appeared and worsened after I spent more time and money at the casino.
basic_info.core_demands: The decisive factor prompting me to seek counseling is realizing that my gambling habit is negatively affecting my mental health and financial stability.
growth_experiences: Experienced a difficult period in personal life a few months ago, starting to visit the casino more frequently to Displace attention, which then developed into spending most time at the casino, spending beyond limits, leading to neglected daily responsibilities and Interpersonal relationships, and generating strong shame and self-loathing after leaving each time having lost money.
Limited information about the family of origin, only knowing Mother works as a palm reader in New Orleans, other caregivers or family structure Not mentioned.

special_situations.event: Leaving after losing money at the casino each time
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I lose money, it means I am a failure and have no value
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduces contact with friends, conceals recent situations to avoid being evaluated or humiliated

special_situations.event: Exceeds the spending limit set for gambling
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am unable to strictly control spending, it means I have no self-control and am very useless
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Comforting oneself with 'this time will be different, I can win it back', continuing to raise bets to try to recover losses
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This time will be different; I can win back the money I lost

special_situations.event: When feeling particularly low or stressed
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: I must distract myself by going to the casino, otherwise emotions will spiral out of control and be unbearable
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Uses gambling as a way of emotional escape and self-soothing
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I feel terrible now; going to the casino would help

special_situations.event: When thinking of friends, worrying about being asked about his situation or compared
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If they knew my current gambling situation, they would despise me and distance themselves from me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding contact with friends, Reduced socializing to dodge possible evaluation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will surely look down on me

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be understood and accepted, to maintain self-esteem and a sense of value
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being humiliated for losing control and failing, Being rejected, relationship breakdown
defense_goal: Reduces the risk of being judged and humiliated by avoiding intimate disclosure
Numbing painful emotions with gambling to temporarily reduce Anxiety and shame
Preempts with self-criticism to avoid more painful accusations from outside

object_relations.object_representation: Others (friends / significant others) are harsh judges, people who will be disappointed

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites discussion of 'what was happening in your personal life when gambling started to increase'
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Disclosing details will lead to being judged and losing face, the sense of safety is threatened (transference: regarding others as judges)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Replying politely and briefly, avoiding specific details, reserved tone, quickly Displacing topics.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: At the beginning stage of counseling, invited to believe the conversation may help and to begin cognitive restructuring
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing 'talking does not help me', seeing the counselor as an ineffective helper for self-protection (transference: suspicion of authority)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Downplaying the necessity of change with seemingly rational reasons (e.g. 'talking about it is useless'), cold and skeptical tone.

manifestations: Repeatedly trying to set limits but unable to control spending
Aware of the consequences of gambling choices but finds it hard to take responsibility and change
outcomes: Financial imbalance and neglected daily responsibilities

manifestations: Tense relationships with friends, rarely meeting
Not yet disclosing the gambling problem to friends due to shame
outcomes: Social Withdrawal and the support system not yet activated
Worsening cycles of shame and self-deprecation

manifestations: Stating no longer enjoying gambling, yet continuing to visit the casino habitually
outcomes: Negative attitude, hard to see a way out

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact, corresponding to 'acceptance'.
manifestations: Expressing unwillingness to discuss details when probed about 'what happened in personal life', staying vague instead
Maintains generalized skepticism about change and counseling effects, avoiding going deep into present experience

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Repeated self-deprecation ('I am a failure/loser' 'I have always been harsh on myself')
Worrying about being unable to change in counseling and holding back expression

contact_model.definition: The individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Turning dissatisfaction with the predicament and pressure into self-blame and shame
Not seeking support from friends, turning energy back to bearing it alone

positive_force: Aware that gambling has harmed mental health and finances, with problem insight and motivation to change
Willing to try counseling and cognitive restructuring, even while skeptical
Able to recognize some triggering factors (more likely to visit the casino When feeling low or stressed)
Has potential social support (has friends to talk with)
Aware that gambling no longer brings pleasure, with a realistic basis for re-choosing
negative_force: Self-labeling and Self-deprecation ('I am a failure') reinforcing shame and helplessness
Uses gambling as a habitual strategy for emotional escape, hard to interrupt
Cognitive biases (predicting the future / Fantasizing about 'winning back losses') maintaining continued betting
Shame hindering help-seeking and disclosure, leaving Social support not yet activated
Skeptical toward counseling and change, reducing engagement in action

target_behavior.behavior: Gambling at casinos for long hours and over budget
antecedent: Forming a fixed habit of going to casinos
When near or over the set limit
target_behavior.core_reason: Using gambling as a strategy to escape negative emotions and stress, holding the expectation of 'winning back the losses' to restore a sense of control and self-esteem
target_behavior.function: Escaping unwelcome emotional experiences, gaining brief excitement and hope
target_behavior.consequence: Neglected daily responsibilities, Tense relationships with friends, unstable finances, worsened shame and self-loathing after leaving the casino

target_behavior.behavior: Self-belittlement and shame (repeatedly labeling herself a 'failure')
antecedent: When losing money and leaving the casino
target_behavior.core_reason: The internalized core belief of 'I am very useless / I am a failure' being activated in failure situations
target_behavior.function: Explains loss of control and failure through self-blame, briefly avoids facing actions for change and interpersonal evaluation
target_behavior.consequence: The negative emotional cycle intensifies, further avoiding seeking help and numbing emotions with gambling
